$comment: Every secret and variable a connector stack needs, with who owns it.
owner=generated: bootstrap mints it with crypto.randomBytes and writes it to the stack's GitHub Environment. Nobody ever types it.
owner=operator: a root credential a human provides ONCE. Bootstrap only verifies that it is present.
owner=module: an output another module writes back after it runs (a Logto app upsert, a minted certificate, an agent enrollment). Not required before that module has run.
scope=stack: one value per stack, in that stack's GitHub Environment.

scope=host: shared by the stacks that share a Postgres instance (bank-prod + shop-prod; bank-staging + shop-staging). A host-scoped secret carrying a `service` field belongs only to that service's environments; one without it must hold the same value in both, because it describes the shared instance itself.
scope=global: repository-level, shared by every stack.
scope=consumer: written into the CONSUMER's environment and never into a connector's. A connector holding one of these would defeat the property it exists to provide.

rendersTo: a stack's GitHub Environment names secrets unprefixed, because an environment belongs to exactly one service. A host that runs both services renders one env file, so the renderer prefixes with BANK_ / SHOP_ on the way out. <SVC> is that prefix.
Drift between this manifest and a GitHub Environment fails `iac.yml` in verify mode, loudly.

secrets.name: BUNDLE_SEAL_KEY_K1
secrets.purpose: AES-256-GCM key that seals session bundles. 32 bytes, base64. The only thing standing between a bundle on a user's device and their credentials.
secrets.rotation: Never in place. Rotation is a kid bump: mint K2, point BUNDLE_CURRENT_KID at it, leave K1 in the ring until every bundle sealed under it has passed its TTL, then blank it. No mass re-login event, ever.

secrets.name: BUNDLE_SEAL_KEY_K2
secrets.purpose: The next seal key. Absent until a rotation starts; an empty entry is ignored by the host.
secrets.rotation: See BUNDLE_SEAL_KEY_K1. K3 replaces K1's slot on the following rotation.

secrets.name: VAULT_KEK
secrets.purpose: Wraps the per-connection DEKs used by `server` custody. Required only when features.vault is on, which is only legal where a provider can genuinely run unattended.
secrets.rotation: On demand; re-wraps every stored DEK. Never in the database, and never in the same place as the ciphertext it protects.

secrets.name: AGENT_ENROLLMENT_HMAC
secrets.purpose: Signs the one-time agent enrollment codes. The code carries the subject, which is what stops an enrolled BYO agent from ever serving anyone but the user who enrolled it.
secrets.rotation: On demand. Invalidates unredeemed codes only - already-issued agent tokens keep working.

secrets.name: WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY
secrets.purpose: HMAC-SHA256 over `t.body` for the payload-free webhooks to the consumer. The same value is written to the consumer as CONNECTOR_<SVC>_WEBHOOK_KEY.
secrets.rotation: Coordinated: both sides must move together, so rotate during a window where a few dropped events cost nothing. Events are notifications, not data; the consumer always pulls.

secrets.name: MTLS_CA_CERT
secrets.purpose: The internal CA that signs the consumer's client certificate. The connector rejects any /v1/* call without a certificate this CA issued, which is what stops a compromised container on the same network.
secrets.rotation: Long-lived (5y). Rotating it means re-issuing the consumer's client cert in the same change; do it deliberately, not on a schedule.

secrets.name: MTLS_CA_KEY
secrets.purpose: The CA's private key. Held only by the IaC bootstrap; never mounted into a running container.
secrets.rotation: With MTLS_CA_CERT. A leak here means anyone can mint a client cert the connector trusts, so it is the one key that justifies re-issuing everything.

secrets.name: MTLS_SERVER_CERT
secrets.purpose: The control plane's own TLS certificate, signed by MTLS_CA_CERT. Rendered to deploy/env/tls/server.crt.pem.
secrets.rotation: Yearly, or whenever the hostname changes. A restart picks it up.

secrets.name: MTLS_SERVER_KEY
secrets.purpose: Private key for MTLS_SERVER_CERT. Rendered to deploy/env/tls/server.key.pem as a file, not an environment variable - environment shows up in `docker inspect` and in every crash dump.
secrets.rotation: With MTLS_SERVER_CERT.

secrets.name: CONSUMER_CLIENT_CERT_FINGERPRINT
secrets.purpose: SHA-256 fingerprint of the one client certificate allowed to call /v1/*. Written back by the mTLS module after it mints the consumer's cert. Pinned, not merely CA-validated: a CA that can issue one client cert can issue two.
secrets.rotation: Whenever the consumer's client certificate is re-issued. Both values move in the same apply.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_M2M_APP_ID
secrets.purpose: Logto machine-to-machine application for this connector, written back after the upsert. The connector needs the id to check that a token's client matches the session's client; it does not need the secret.
secrets.rotation: Stable. Changing it severs every session, because authorisation is `token.client == session.client`.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_M2M_APP_SECRET
secrets.purpose: The M2M client secret. Written back by the module and forwarded to the consumer as CONNECTOR_<SVC>_M2M_APP_SECRET; the connector itself never uses it.
secrets.rotation: On demand in Logto, then re-run the apply so the consumer's environment follows.

secrets.name: AGENT_TOKEN_NAS_HTTP
secrets.purpose: Per-agent bearer token for the http-tier pooled agent, scoped to /agent/v1/* and nothing else. Written back after the agent redeems its enrollment code.
secrets.rotation: Revoke and re-enrol. Revoking one agent's token affects only that agent.

secrets.name: AGENT_TOKEN_HOME_BROWSER
secrets.purpose: Per-agent bearer token for the residential browser agent. Lives on that box, never on the NAS.
secrets.rotation: Revoke and re-enrol.

secrets.name: CANARY_CREDENTIALS_JSON
secrets.purpose: Credentials for the dedicated per-provider test accounts the canary runs use. Real accounts, never a real user's - a canary that locks someone out is worse than no canary.
secrets.rotation: Whenever a canary account's own credentials change.

secrets.name: POSTGRES_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD
secrets.purpose: Postgres superuser. Used by initdb to create the per-service roles and by nobody else - neither control plane ever connects as it.
secrets.rotation: On demand; requires ALTER ROLE on the running instance in the same change.

secrets.name: POSTGRES_BANK_PASSWORD
secrets.purpose: Login for the bank_connector role. That role cannot connect to the shop database at all (deploy/initdb), so a leak here reaches bank sessions and nothing else.
secrets.rotation: On demand; ALTER ROLE plus a redeploy of the bank control plane.

secrets.name: POSTGRES_SHOP_PASSWORD
secrets.purpose: Login for the shop_connector role. Cannot connect to the bank database.
secrets.rotation: On demand; ALTER ROLE plus a redeploy of the shop control plane.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_DOMAIN
secrets.purpose: The DDNS domain the stacks hang their hostnames off. A secret only because this repository is public.
secrets.rotation: Never casually - it appears in the server certificates.

secrets.name: IAC_GH_PAT
secrets.purpose: Fine-grained PAT for this repository with Administration + Secrets + Variables read/write. Bootstrap writes environment secrets, which GITHUB_TOKEN cannot do.
secrets.rotation: Yearly, or immediately on any suspicion. It can rewrite every generated secret in the repo.

secrets.name: GHCR_PAT
secrets.purpose: Fine-grained PAT with read:packages, so the NAS can pull the images.
secrets.rotation: Yearly. Read-only, so the blast radius is 'someone can pull our images'.

secrets.name: LOGTO_INFRA_M2M_ID
secrets.purpose: The one manual auth step: an M2M application with the Logto Management API role, created once by hand. Everything else about Logto is code.
secrets.rotation: On demand in the Logto admin console.

secrets.name: LOGTO_INFRA_M2M_SECRET
secrets.purpose: Secret for LOGTO_INFRA_M2M_ID.
secrets.rotation: See LOGTO_INFRA_M2M_ID.

secrets.name: SYNOLOGY_URL
secrets.purpose: DSM endpoint for the deploy module. Optional because the stacks set network.reverseProxy = false: nothing here needs the DSM API unless that changes.
secrets.rotation: n/a

secrets.name: SYNOLOGY_USER
secrets.purpose: DSM account used to place the rendered stack on the NAS.
secrets.rotation: On demand.

secrets.name: SYNOLOGY_PASS
secrets.purpose: Password for SYNOLOGY_USER.
secrets.rotation: On demand.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_BANK_SUBJECT_SALT
secrets.purpose: HMAC key the consumer uses to mint the pseudonymous subject it sends to the bank connector. Held ONLY by the consumer: if a connector held its own salt it could map a subject back to a person, which is the exact property this design buys.
secrets.rotation: Rotating it severs every bank connection at once - which is precisely why it exists as a clean kill switch for one service.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_SHOP_SUBJECT_SALT
secrets.purpose: The same, for the shopping connector. A separate salt is what stops the two connectors from telling that a bank subject and a shop subject are the same human, even if both databases leaked.
secrets.rotation: Severs every shopping connection. Independent of the bank salt, deliberately.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_BANK_WEBHOOK_KEY
secrets.purpose: The consumer's copy of the bank connector's WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY, for verifying inbound event signatures.
secrets.rotation: With WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY, in the same apply.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_SHOP_WEBHOOK_KEY
secrets.purpose: The consumer's copy of the shopping connector's WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY.
secrets.rotation: With WEBHOOK_SIGNING_KEY, in the same apply.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_BANK_M2M_APP_ID
secrets.purpose: The consumer's client id for the bank connector's M2M application.
secrets.rotation: With CONNECTOR_M2M_APP_ID.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_BANK_M2M_APP_SECRET
secrets.purpose: The consumer's client secret for the bank connector's M2M application.
secrets.rotation: With CONNECTOR_M2M_APP_SECRET.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_SHOP_M2M_APP_ID
secrets.purpose: The consumer's client id for the shopping connector's M2M application.
secrets.rotation: With CONNECTOR_M2M_APP_ID.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_SHOP_M2M_APP_SECRET
secrets.purpose: The consumer's client secret for the shopping connector's M2M application.
secrets.rotation: With CONNECTOR_M2M_APP_SECRET.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_BANK_CLIENT_CERT_PEM
secrets.purpose: Client certificate the consumer presents to the bank connector, signed by that stack's MTLS_CA_CERT and pinned by fingerprint.
secrets.rotation: With CONSUMER_CLIENT_CERT_FINGERPRINT, in the same apply, or the consumer locks itself out.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_BANK_CLIENT_KEY_PEM
secrets.purpose: Private key for CONNECTOR_BANK_CLIENT_CERT_PEM.
secrets.rotation: With the certificate.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_SHOP_CLIENT_CERT_PEM
secrets.purpose: Client certificate the consumer presents to the shopping connector. A separate certificate from the bank one on purpose: one compromised client must not open both services.
secrets.rotation: With CONSUMER_CLIENT_CERT_FINGERPRINT, in the same apply.

secrets.name: CONNECTOR_SHOP_CLIENT_KEY_PEM
secrets.purpose: Private key for CONNECTOR_SHOP_CLIENT_CERT_PEM.
secrets.rotation: With the certificate.

variables.name: CONNECTOR_REGISTRY
variables.purpose: Image registry, e.g. ghcr.io/okkes. A variable rather than a literal so a fork or a local registry needs no code change.

variables.name: BUNDLE_CURRENT_KID
variables.purpose: Which seal key new bundles use. The one value a rotation actually flips.

variables.name: LAN_BIND_IP
variables.purpose: The address the control plane's port is bound to. 0.0.0.0 here would silently undo the lan-only exposure the stack file declares, so the compose file has no default for it.

variables.name: AUTH_AUTHORITY
variables.purpose: OIDC issuer that mints the consumer's M2M tokens.

variables.name: M2M_AUDIENCE
variables.purpose: Audience the M2M token must carry, checked alongside the connector.bank / connector.shop scope.

variables.name: WEBHOOK_URL
variables.purpose: Where the payload-free events go. The only outbound call a connector makes to the consumer, and it carries no data.
